why: The array index as the hash: every value lies in 1..n-1, so each value names a slot of the array itself. Mark slot v by negating it the first time you see v; meeting a slot that is already negative means v was seen before.
hints: A set solves it in O(n) extra space. The values are in 1..n-1 and the array has n slots. Can the array itself be the set?
Use the sign of nums[v] as a 'seen v' flag. Since all values are positive, negating does not destroy the value stored there (take abs when you read it).
For each x: v = abs(x); if nums[v] < 0 return v; else nums[v] = -nums[v]. O(n) time, O(1) extra space (work on a copy if the caller's array must stay intact).
pitfalls: Read abs(x): the element you are visiting may itself have been negated earlier.
Index 0 is never used as a mark because values start at 1; that is fine.
Floyd's cycle detection is the follow-up when the array must not be modified at all.
